I wonder why it is supposed to be better to poll rather than using `select()`?

> I wonder why it is supposed to be better to poll rather than using `select()`?

Searching the internet for "select versus poll" will give you answers, for example:
[https://devarea.com/linux-io-multiplexing-select-vs-poll-vs-epoll/](https://devarea.com/linux-io-multiplexing-select-vs-poll-vs-epoll/) or [https://daniel.haxx.se/docs/poll-vs-select.html](https://daniel.haxx.se/docs/poll-vs-select.html)

`select()` is inefficient and limited to a maximum of `FD_SETSIZE` file descriptors (Linux kernel by default sets this to 1024).

Thank you for the explanation and the pointers with interesting further detail!

issue_context.title: Why select() in BIO_socket_wait()? Please avoid using select() anywhere!
issue_context.body:
Hi!

select() only works if the number of possible open file descriptors is below FD_SETSIZE. We need to run our application with a higher value (ulimit -n ...) so we might run into problems if BIO_socket_wait() is called with such a high file descriptor.

Not calling BIO_socket_wait() or BIO_wait() is no option as it might be called within OpenSSL which is not under our control.

So, please replace any select() by poll().

Regards,
Andreas

review_comments: This should probably use ossl_time_now instead of time directly.  The select code likely should too, but that quite old code.
You might be right, but IMHO this should be addressed in another (separate) commit as it would require more changes if time_t is replaced by OSSL_TIME.
I agree with both - the interface to `BIO_socket_wait()` uses `time_t`, so any changes to use ossl_time should be done separately
